title: User space and the kernel: what CUDA++ replaces and what it still needs
summary: Drake built CUDA++ by cutting at the user-space/kernel line: everything closed above NVIDIA's open kernel module (nvcc, PTX, libcudart, libcuda, cuBLAS) is replaced by his own encoder and runtime, which talk to nvidia.ko and nvidia-uvm.ko through ioctls on /dev/nvidiactl, /dev/nvidia0 and /dev/nvidia-uvm. What stays NVIDIA's: the open kernel module (580.173.02 only) and the signed GSP firmware. I can show you the grep that proves the line, including the one interop probe that links libcuda on purpose.
goal: Know which parts of the CUDA stack run in your process and which in the kernel, and what CUDA++ still depends on.
key_steps: List the layers: compiler, runtime, driver library, kernel module, firmware.
Find the device files the driver client opens.
Confirm the library links no CUDA library (and find the one interop tool that does).
Name what stays NVIDIA: the open kernel module version and the signed firmware.
Check the evidence state before claiming the path works on a GPU.

example.code:
#!/bin/sh
# Lesson cuda-01: where the line between user space and the kernel runs in CUDApp, read from the
# pinned sources with grep (an inspection, no first-party logic, no device opened).
set -u
export LC_ALL=C
SRC=${SRC:?set SRC to a directory holding the clones in docs/learn/teach/PINS}
OMC=${OMC:-$SRC/omega-mv/seed/out/omc}
PIN=befb8199db8c4bca188a494dfaac2a6f0ee5c36fcea11188c75666c55fce8a1d
got=$(sha256sum "$OMC" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-64)
if [ "$got" != "$PIN" ]; then
    echo "omc sha256 mismatch: refusing to run"
    exit 90
fi
echo "omc sha256 $PIN (not needed by this inspection; checked so every lesson pins the same tools)"
C=$SRC/CUDApp
cd "$C" || exit 2

echo "== 1. the build promise (Makefile header)"
grep -n 'no CUDA toolkit, no NVIDIA user-space library' Makefile

echo "== 2. files that include a CUDA header or link libcuda (first-party C, Makefile, mk/)"
git grep -l '#include <cuda\|#include "cuda\|-lcuda' -- '*.c' '*.h' Makefile mk
echo "   the Makefile line that links it, and the target it belongs to:"
grep -n -- '-lcuda' Makefile | cut -c1-120

echo "== 3. the three device files the driver client opens (kernel entry points)"
grep -n '"/dev/nvidia' nvrm/nvrm.c native/nvrm/context.om

echo "== 4. what came from the kernel side: the open module's headers, by folder"
cd third_party/nvidia-open-580.173.02 || exit 2
for d in kernel-open/common/inc kernel-open/nvidia-uvm src/common/sdk/nvidia/inc src/nvidia/arch/nvalloc/unix/include; do
    echo "   $(find "$d" -name '*.h' | wc -l | tr -d ' ') headers in $d"
done
echo "   $(grep -c '\.h$' SHA256SUMS) headers listed in SHA256SUMS"
cd "$C" || exit 2

echo "== 5. what still belongs to NVIDIA below the line (ROADMAP.md)"
grep -n '^| `nvidia.ko`\|^| `nvidia-uvm.ko`\|^| GSP firmware' ROADMAP.md | cut -d'|' -f2,4,5

== 5. what still belongs to NVIDIA below the line (ROADMAP.md)
 `nvidia.ko` | AIEN's own GB10 driver (L332) | BUILDING 
 `nvidia-uvm.ko` | same driver: GPU page tables, allocator, channels (L193 cut D, L332) | BUILDING 
 GSP firmware (`gsp_*.bin`) | stays NVIDIA's: the chip checks its signature | not replaceable

common_mistake: Saying CUDA++ uses no NVIDIA software. It uses no NVIDIA user-space software at run time; the open kernel module (one pinned version) and the signed GSP firmware are still NVIDIA's. Say exactly that.
